{{1976 Pacific-8 Conference football standings}}
The '''1976 Oregon State Beavers football team''' represented [[Oregon State University]] as a member of the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pacific-8 Conference]] (Pac-8) during the [[1976 NCAA Division I football season]]. In their first season under head coach [[Craig Fertig]], the Beavers compiled an overall record of 2–10 with a mark of 1–6 in conference play, placing last out of eight teams in the Pac-8, and were outscored<!-- by their opponents,--> 325 to 179.<ref>{{cite web|title=1976 Oregon State Beavers Schedule and Results|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=SR/College Football|access-date=September 7, 2016|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon-state/1976-schedule.html}}</ref> The team played its five home games on campus at [[Parker Stadium]] in [[Corvallis, Oregon|Corvallis]].<ref name=endhappy>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=ta5hAAAAIBAJ&sjid=9uADAAAAIBAJ&pg=3315%2C5014205 |work=Eugene Register-Guard |last=Withers |first=Bud |title=Oregon makes the ending happy, 23–14 |date=November 21, 1976 |page=1C}}</ref>

Fertig, age 34, was previously an assistant coach as the [[University of Southern California]] (USC) and a quarterback for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]] under [[John McKay (American football)|John McKay]]. He succeeded [[Dee Andros]] in December 1975 with a three-year contract at $26,000 per year.<ref name=fttscdee>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=WK5VAAAAIBAJ&sjid=POADAAAAIBAJ&pg=6162%2C3600163| newspaper=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon|last=Conrad |first=John |title=Fertig tapped to succeed Dee |date=December 12, 1975 |page=1B }}</ref><ref name=fgbp>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=xzYwAAAAIBAJ&sjid=zvgDAAAAIBAJ&pg=4422%2C4103029 |work=Spokane Daily Chronicle |location=Washington|title=Fertig gets Beaver post |agency=Associated Press |date=December 12, 1975 |page=24}}</ref>
